text:
Maya R.: Heads-up — we need a quick sync on the analytics schema change for per-tenant quota bucketing.
Chris L.: ack. quick context?
Maya R.: currently quotas are attached to route_id. proposal: introduce tenant_bucket_id and map quotas to buckets to reduce cardinality and make dashboard aggregation cheaper.
Alex P.: sounds sensible. what's the migration plan?
Maya R.: idea: add nullable tenant_bucket_id col to events table, dual-write from API for 6 weeks, backfill historical events in batches, then make col non-null and switch console queries to use bucket_id.
Sophia N.: main risks I see: backfill time + IO on hot partitions, and dashboards that join on route_id will break until we update them. also index bloat.
Chris L.: can we do shadow-reads in console first? keep route_id fallback during rollout.
Maya R.: yes — console will prefer bucket_id when present, else fallback to route_id. plan to flip hard after all rows backfilled.
Jin (infra-bot): note: adding a new indexed col on events_recent partition will incur a reindex if we want fast reads. consider a partial index or using bloom filter.
Alex P.: partial index on events_recent where tenant_bucket_id is not null? creates uneven performance while backfill runs.
Sophia N.: suggestion: create col, populate values for new writes only (zero-downtime), create index on (tenant_bucket_id, day), backfill during low-traffic windows to avoid CPU spikes.
Chris L.: can we break backfill into tenant shards and run per-tenant transactions? throttled via rate limiter.
Maya R.: yes. propose a backfill job that picks tenant ranges and writes in 5k row batches with 30ms sleep between batches. script will report progress to #eng-platform-migrations.
Alex P.: SQL sample please.
Maya R.: ```sql
ALTER TABLE analytics.events ADD COLUMN tenant_bucket_id uuid;
UPDATE analytics.events SET tenant_bucket_id = map_bucket(tenant_id) WHERE tenant_bucket_id IS NULL LIMIT 5000;
```
Chris L.: map_bucket() is our mapping function in pg? we probably want an immutable mapping table instead so backfill is deterministic.
Maya R.: agreed — we'll maintain tenant_bucket_map table and reference it in the UPDATE join.
Sophia N.: what about partitioning? new index per partition may be heavy. we could backfill older partitions cold (offline) and only index the hot partitions.
Alex P.: for queries: dashboards need a compatibility view. create analytics.view_route_or_bucket that returns a canonical bucket_key we can use in existing aggregation queries.
Maya R.: yes — view will be our migration shim. we'll change the console to use the view and gradually retire route-based aggregations.
Jin (infra-bot): deployment note: rolling deploy required. ensure new API version is dual-write capable before starting backfill.
Chris L.: rollout phases?
Maya R.: Phase 0: schema change + deploy dual-write API to staging. Phase 1: enable dual-write in prod for new traffic. Phase 2: start backfill per-tenant shards. Phase 3: switch console to view_route_or_bucket. Phase 4: make tenant_bucket_id NOT NULL + drop old route-only paths.
Sophia N.: canary idea: backfill a small set of high-traffic tenants first and validate dashboard numbers vs baseline.
Alex P.: validation checks: total tokens, event counts per day, 95th-latency for analytics queries, and dashboard card snapshots.
Maya R.: add an automated regression alert: if per-tenant daily counts differ >0.5% from baseline after switch, auto-fallback to route-based queries for that tenant.
Chris L.: auth/permissions: any console changes must respect existing per-tenant scoping. view shim should not leak cross-tenant data.
Maya R.: good call. tenant_bucket_map will include tenant_id -> bucket_id and be multi-tenant aware; view will filter by tenant_id.
Jin (infra-bot): reminder: schedule a maintenance window for reindexing hot partitions in case we need to rebuild.
Alex P.: docs: runbook, smoke tests, rollback steps, and cost estimate for IO during backfill. I can draft the runbook.
Maya R.: assigning tasks: Alex — runbook + validation queries. Chris — backfill runner (k8s job) + throttling. Sophia — console view integration + canary dashboards. I'll own mapping table and rollout coordination.
Chris L.: ETA?
Maya R.: aiming for staging deploy this week, prod dual-write next Tue, backfill 2 weeks after if metrics look good.
Sophia N.: tagging: @analytics-team for dashboard changes. also mention support for customers who care about historical quota windows.
Alex P.: one more: for large tenants we might want to do targeted snapshot backfills (export/import) instead of row-by-row UPDATE. saves time.
Maya R.: noted. we'll detect big tenants and route them to export/import pipeline.
Chris L.: ok — I'll prototype the runner and post results to the thread.
Maya R.: thanks. logging to #eng-platform-migrations and I'll create a short playbook in the runbook repo. :thumbsup:
